title: U.S. Military to Cut 20% of Its Generals and Admirals
summary:
U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth gave a speech on Wednesday at Marine Corps Base Quantico in Virginia. He called it a "state of the force" address. He spoke to junior officers and enlisted leaders.

Hegseth said the military will cut 20% of its generals and admirals. Last spring, he ordered a 10% cut to about 800 top officer positions. Now he has told all the military services to double that cut. The work is to be finished by Jan. 1, 2027. "I call it accountability and long overdue," he said.

He also announced a new four-star command. It will oversee autonomous and robotic tools for the military. Hegseth called this "the fastest peacetime shift in modern military history." He named a group to study the future of warfare, too. It will be led by Elon Musk, former House Speaker Newt Gingrich and Palmer Luckey, a co-founder of Anduril Industries.

Two senators had different reactions. Democratic Sen. Mark Kelly, a former navy combat pilot, said, "He's purging a generation of great leaders of the military, and it's going to take a generation to recover from it." Republican Sen. Mike Rounds said he wanted to understand Hegseth's reasoning. He said, "I want to see it first."

The speech came seven months into a war with Iran. The U.S. and Iran are also in a stalemate over the Strait of Hormuz, an important shipping route for energy.
why_it_matters: It shows how leaders of the military and members of Congress can have different views about big changes to who leads the armed forces.
